headline: High: Copilot can read and write repo context while the paired open-source list offers no isolation, creating default data-leak and conflict risk; prompt-injection risk is limited by the list’s non-runnable nature.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest or execute prompts. Agent B reads editor buffers and repo context and can propose edits, but the pair lacks a direct shared channel beyond manual transfer. That makes prompt injection possible mainly through copied content, not a default automated bridge.
conditions: IF a human copies content from Agent A into Agent B chat or editor buffers, injection becomes possible.
IF Agent B is configured to ingest arbitrary repo text as instructions, malicious text can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep Agent A content out of Copilot chat unless reviewed.
Use a strict prompt template that labels pasted text as untrusted.
Review any generated edits before applying them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for pasted snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read filesystem content and repo context and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while Agent A is a public open-source list with no sensitive-data handling. The pair therefore creates a default path for source-code leakage from B’s workspace to a third-party backend; A does not add protection or isolation.
conditions: IF sensitive source code is present in Agent B's open editor buffers or repo context, it may be transmitted to Copilot's backend.
IF the workspace contains secrets, those secrets can enter B's inference context.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before using Copilot.
Limit Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Close unrelated files before prompting.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning pre-commit hooks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Agent A is a static open-source list with no write controls. If both are used around the same repo, B can create conflicting edits or git changes without any locking shown in either profile. The uncertainty about orchestration means we should not down-rank this.
conditions: IF Agent B is pointed at a repository that a human also edits, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Agent B applies Workspace edits while another process changes git state, divergence can occur.
mitigations: Pause other editors before applying Copilot edits.
Review diffs before commit.
Use one writer per repo at a time.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge coordination.
requires-engineering: isolate Copilot to a scratch branch.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can turn generated suggestions into edits, and its Workspace mode proposes applied changes for human review. Agent A contributes no verification layer, so if A-derived content is pasted into B, B may propagate it into code or commits. This is not high because human review exists, but the default workflow still allows unverified cascade.
conditions: IF a user pastes Agent A output into Agent B, B may treat it as authoritative context.
IF Workspace edits are accepted without review, incorrect content can propagate into code.
mitigations: Verify generated changes against source material.
Reject edits that cite untrusted pasted text.
Use human review for every applied patch.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B has GitHub repo OAuth scope and sends context to a vendor API, while Agent A is a public open-source list with no data residency or retention commitments in the profile. The main compliance issue is limited to using B on regulated or sensitive repositories; A does not itself process regulated data, so only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Agent B's repo context, vendor processing may create policy mismatch.
IF the repository contains data subject to stricter residency or retention rules, Copilot use may violate them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Copilot-enabled repos.
Check internal policy before enabling Copilot.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: document a DPA/residency review for the workspace.
